decision: built two domain services plus an engine rather than one service
why: the value is the boundary between services that own state and an engine that only proposes
result: accepted by reviewer

decision: workflows are data, not code
why: the ask is a builder where customers compose workflows, so the engine has to compile a saved definition
result: green tests

decision: enforced platform invariants in the validator
why: user-authored automation that can move pay without a human is the failure mode worth designing out
result: 30 tests pass

decision: Bun plus Elysia plus Eden on Postgres
why: Drizzle keeps the runtime free of native binaries and Eden gives the UI the server's types
result: typecheck clean

decision: event backbone behind a port, Redis Streams locally
why: one broker for the demo while keeping consumer groups, replay, and per-tenant ordering
result: verified by e2e

decision: BullMQ for execution and LangGraph for the graph
why: approval latency must not depend on worker lifetime, and retries and DLQ stay ours
result: verified by e2e

decision: transactional outbox with skinny events
why: avoids the dual-write bug and matches the skinny webhooks Humanforce HR already emits
result: verified by tests and e2e

decision: wrote contracts and the DSL before any service
why: the five build slices compile against one interface instead of negotiating
result: 30 tests pass

decision: canvas geometry stored as layout beside the DSL
why: React Flow positions are UI metadata and must not leak into the executable definition
result: implemented

decision: proved the outbox and the Redis backbone against real infra
why: these carry the at-least-once and dedupe claims, so they cannot rest on a mock
result: 37 tests pass

decision: studio migrations as plain SQL applied by a tracked migrator
why: a reviewer can read the schema in a diff and a rerun is a no-op
result: 9 tables created

decision: env files symlinked into each workspace
why: bun and next read .env from their own cwd, and one source of truth beats four
result: env resolves in service cwd

decision: workflows became a DSL with a validator and a compiler
why: the approved ask is a drag-and-drop builder, which needs definitions the engine compiles
result: green

decision: five slices built in parallel against frozen contracts
why: the interfaces were done first, so services, engine, and UI could be written without negotiating
result: 94 package and service tests pass

decision: found the stalled runs were BullMQ rejecting job ids containing ":"
why: every enqueue threw after the dedupe row was written, so runs sat queued forever
result: 8/8 e2e pass

decision: made redelivery re-enqueue stranded queued runs
why: a failed enqueue could otherwise lose a run permanently despite at-least-once delivery
result: recovery path coded

decision: an employee cancelling now vacates the shift instead of cancelling it
why: the coverage workflow must be able to fill the shift the sick employee vacated, and the service refused offers on a cancelled shift
result: tests updated, 21 pass

decision: outbox payloads bind as objects, seed payloads bind as text then cast
why: the driver stores a JSON string as a jsonb string scalar, while an object binds correctly, and the outbox reads the payload back as text and parses it
result: declared output verified as object

decision: fixed the overview reading a wrapped workflows object
why: the API returns an array and the page crashed on first load
result: page renders 2 workflows, 3 runs

decision: one timesheet exception event per clock-out, not one per breach
why: two events for one timesheet started two runs, and each run could apply its own stale adjustment
result: 16 attendance tests pass

decision: scripts/verify.sh is the single definition of done
why: infra, migrations, seed, typecheck, four processes, and the scenarios in one command
result: all properties verified

decision: browser-verified the whole loop, not just the API
why: the demo is judged on the UI: canvas, validation block, approval card, live timeline
result: run succeeded, shift status offered

decision: a second engine instance finishes a run parked by the first
why: the checkpoint claim is load bearing, and only Postgres-backed state proves it
result: 1 test passes

decision: added the rejection path to the end-to-end suite
why: the design promised a rejection outcome that no test exercised
result: 8 e2e tests pass

decision: outbox rows poison after a capped number of parse failures
why: a payload that can never parse would otherwise retry for the life of the deployment
result: 5 outbox tests pass

decision: the simulator clocks out at the scheduled shift end, not at wall-clock now
why: clocking out at now invented hours that were never worked, so the overtime the workflow reasoned about did not match the timesheet
result: timesheet reads 509 worked / 29 overtime

decision: replaced postgres.js with Bun's built-in SQL client
why: the client ships with the runtime we already deploy, and removing the package deleted two driver workarounds outright
result: 96 package and service tests pass, 8 e2e pass

decision: jsonb columns are declared through a customType that hands the driver the object
why: drizzle's jsonb() stringifies its value and Bun encodes that string a second time, which stored a jsonb string scalar instead of a document
result: jsonb_typeof=object verified for definition, layout, and response after seeding

decision: noted that SQLSTATE is on err.errno, not err.code
why: Bun reports code=ERR_POSTGRES_SERVER_ERROR and puts the SQLSTATE on errno, which is the field to read if anything ever branches on a constraint violation
result: no call sites read SQLSTATE today

decision: bound array and timestamp parameters explicitly after the swap
why: Bun binds a plain JS array as a comma-joined string, and infers an untyped Date parameter as interval in date arithmetic
result: 21 rostering tests pass, 8 e2e pass

decision: ran three independent designs for the node-kind kernel and judged them against a fixed rubric
why: the extension model is a one-way door: every stored workflow depends on it, and my first idea is not evidence
result: base picked: capability registry, with two grafts from the runner-up

decision: verified the union assembly against zod 4 instead of trusting the judge's zod 3 reasoning
why: both leading designs assembled the runtime union with Object.values(registry).map(...), which does not typecheck because zod needs a tuple, and the failure is silent at runtime
result: docs/arena/kernel-synthesis.md, packages/workflows/.scratch (removed)
column7: two workable assemblies proven to compile and narrow; the tuple form chosen

decision: built the feature harness before any feature, and captured the red baseline
why: the check has to read as old versus new, so the baseline is recorded while every property still fails
result: 16 of 16 feature properties fail, each with a specific reason

decision: froze the cross-slice contracts before fanning out
why: three parallel slices write tables the fourth reads, so the shape is fixed first
result: DTOs and three tables landed and migrated

decision: the platform provider is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured from env
why: the user supplies base_url and key once, and every tenant can select it without their own account
result: real call verified: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash returned 200 in 908ms with usage in=81 out=164

decision: only models listed in config/models.jsonl are offered
why: the file is the allow-list, so adding a model is one line and nothing else in the code knows the list
result: loaded at boot, malformed lines rejected with the file and line number

decision: migrated the node kinds onto a capability registry with a single declaration per kind
why: the extension model is the thing a customer's saved workflows depend on, so it was designed by competition and then pinned by a contract test
result: 128 package and service tests pass; inspector shrank from 1025 to 104 lines

decision: single-sourced the {{...}} grammar, resolver, and save-time checker
why: three copies of a template mechanism is how a typo becomes a 3am page, and the checker now walks the event's published JSON Schema
result: unknown paths rejected with TEMPLATE_EVENT_PATH; whole-reference splicing preserved

decision: replaced the LangChain OpenAI SDK with an abstract provider over raw HTTP
why: the feature deleted a dependency instead of adding one, and it puts the vendor's own token counts within reach
result: @langchain/openai removed; 14 provider and settings tests pass

decision: the model catalogue is a JSONL allow-list loaded at boot
why: adding a model must be one line, and a workflow naming anything else is refused at save time with the file named
result: models check passes; UNKNOWN_MODEL diagnostic on save

decision: recorded every model call in llm_calls and priced it from the catalogue
why: the run detail, run list, and dashboard must agree, and the number has to be auditable back to the call
result: token totals equal the SQL sum over llm_calls; dashboard equals SQL aggregates

decision: added the artifact kind as the proof of the extension claim
why: declaring it touched one kind file and two registration lines, and the platform bucketed it by capability rather than by name
result: artifact renders, is listed on the run detail, and is retrievable by id

decision: ran the feature gate against the real vendor, not a fake
why: the provider path is the thing being verified, so the checks point at the configured endpoint and compare tokens against the stored rows
result: all 18 feature properties verified

decision: a reasoning model needed a longer timeout, and a stalled body needed an honest error
why: deepseek-v4.1-flash spent 9030 output tokens to produce a 518 character answer, so the call took 94 seconds and the old 20 second timeout reported it as a malformed body
result: timeout raised to 180s; the error now says the body did not arrive in time

decision: the end-to-end suite runs the deterministic proposer, the feature gate runs the real one
why: the suite asserts fixed outcomes, and the first real-vendor run legitimately failed the award-validity policy check, which is the platform working
result: 8 e2e scenarios pass in 49s; the vendor path is verified separately

decision: applied the shadcn preset bfE7jpo3c to the studio
why: the components were hand-rolled shadcn-style; the preset makes them generated and versioned instead
result: 15 components reinstalled, style radix-lyra, fonts Space Grotesk and Noto Sans

decision: set the dark class on the document root
why: the preset ships a light default and a dark block, and the studio is dark-first, so without it every reinstalled control rendered with light borders on dark surfaces
result: inputs and selects now resolve the preset's dark tokens

decision: imported the React Flow stylesheet from globals.css ahead of our overrides
why: the preset's rewrite moved the cascade so the library's skin beat ours, which turned the minimap into a white box and the edges grey
result: minimap and edge stroke resolve to the studio tokens again; 10 edges render

decision: checked six pages after the preset and cleared the stale local draft
why: the canvas looked empty of edges for a while, which turned out to be a tab loaded mid hot reload plus a leftover draft, not a regression
result: all six pages render with no errors and no white boxes

decision: put the builder chat schemas in @wfm/workflows instead of @wfm/contracts
why: contracts depends on zod alone and must not depend on the DSL, and every chat request carries a full definition and layout
result: one dependency direction kept; the web app already imports DSL types

decision: the model proposes operations from a closed set rather than a whole definition
why: asking a model to reproduce ids, ports, config schemas, and edges every turn means every turn can silently rewrite a part of the graph nobody asked about
result: a bad guess is refused with a reason and the rest of the plan still applies

decision: refused unknown config keys and illegal ports explicitly instead of letting zod strip them
why: zod drops an unknown key silently, which reads to a model as success and teaches it nothing
result: rejection names the keys and ports the kind actually declares

decision: an edit that would leave more validation errors than it started with is dropped whole
why: the studio refuses to store an invalid draft, and a half-applied edit is harder to explain than a refused one
result: adding a node without wiring it is refused with NO_TERMINAL_PATH named

decision: the client sends its current graph with every chat turn
why: the canvas is the system of record including dragged positions, and a server-side session would fight the user for ownership of the canvas
result: the agent reasons about what is on screen, not what it last produced

decision: a decision carries feedback as a separate field from the reason
why: the reason is for the audit trail and the feedback is for the workflow, and merging them would turn every audit sentence into an instruction to a model
result: run.feedback resolves the message and the artifact quotes it

decision: the approval node appends the steering message, not the HTTP decision handler
why: everything before interrupt() re-executes on resume, so a write in the handler and a write in the node would double up
result: one writer, keyed by approval id, so a replayed resume cannot duplicate it

decision: steering reaches the model as an instruction that outranks its default ranking but never a policy check
why: steering is advice about preference, not authority about permission
result: the rules proposer ignores it and says so; the model proposer quotes it

decision: demoed the steering in the coverage artifact body rather than adding a model node after the approval
why: both demo workflows decide before they approve, so a downstream model node would have been a second model call per run for a demo effect
result: the artifact quotes the approver's words verbatim

decision: the feature script's http helper takes a per-call timeout
why: builder chat is a model call and the helper's 20 second default aborted it, which read as a failed property rather than a slow one
result: step 13 passes with a 180 second budget; 20 of 20 properties verified

decision: re-seeded before the feature run instead of trusting the previous state
why: stale demo data made four properties fail for reasons that had nothing to do with the change
result: all 20 properties passed on fresh data

decision: a clean reset now clears the local draft mirror instead of writing it
why: the canvas wrote its own baseline into localStorage on load, so the next load always offered to restore a draft that was never unsaved
result: no banner on a clean load, and a genuine unsaved draft is still offered

decision: a dedicated BuilderRequestError replaces ZodError for provider and catalogue refusals
why: app.ts maps every ZodError to a fixed "Request body failed schema validation", so the actionable reason was buried in details and the panel showed nothing useful
result: the panel now shows the reason itself

decision: resolve the tenant provider before storing the user turn
why: a tenant with no provider or an unlisted model left an unanswered question in the thread and in the next prompt, on every retry
result: zero turns stored on either refusal; a vendor failure still keeps the question, which is the intended case

decision: refuse a per-turn model from the other provider family
why: catalogue membership alone let an anthropic tenant send an openai-compatible id to its own vendor and get an opaque 404
result: 422 naming the family; the panel lists only the family it can use

decision: applyExternal adopts an agent graph as unsaved work
why: reset() cleared the undo stack and never wrote the mirror, so a crash inside the autosave window lost the turn and the user could not undo it
result: mirror carries 10 nodes after a turn and Cmd+Z returns the graph to 9

decision: dropped the note field from the operation schema and the prompt
why: every operation accepted an annotation nothing read, so a model that used it sent dead bytes every turn
result: the contract is six shapes with no unused field

decision: the Redis Streams bus runs on Bun's own client instead of ioredis
why: same reasoning as the SQL client: the runtime already speaks the protocol, and a driver package in our tree is weight we own
result: ioredis is gone from both package.json files; the bus tests pass unchanged

decision: the stream commands go through the client's raw send
why: Bun types most Redis commands but not XADD, XREADGROUP, XACK, XGROUP or XAUTOCLAIM
result: XADD with MAXLEN ~, XGROUP CREATE MKSTREAM, a 1s blocking XREADGROUP, XACK and XAUTOCLAIM all verified against the running broker

decision: noted that Bun hands back a stream read as an object keyed by stream, where ioredis hands back nested arrays
why: the consume loop iterates Object.values(reply) rather than tuples, which is the one behavioural difference the rewrite had to absorb
result: the same consume loop passes the delivery, redelivery and dead-letter tests

decision: BullMQ is given connection options rather than a client
why: BullMQ needs its own blocking connection and ioredis is its dependency, so we stop constructing one and stop declaring the package
result: one fewer direct dependency, and the queue and worker no longer share a socket

decision: the router uses one consumer name per process, not one per subscription
why: the scan re-subscribes per tenant and every subscription minted a fresh name, so the group had accumulated 54 idle consumers whose pending lists a reclaim has to walk
result: one consumer, stable across scans, with the 54 stale ones removed and pending still 0

decision: corrected ADR-0001, which claimed the code runs unchanged on node
why: using Bun.SQL and Bun.redis makes that false, and a stale portability claim is worse than either answer
result: the ADR now states the trade and names which libraries keep their own driver

decision: the builder is canvas-first with floating chrome
why: every surface was docked, so the graph paid for the panels; the reference puts the graph first and lets the panels float over it
result: 9 nodes and 10 edges render on a full-bleed canvas with the rail, panels, pill, and zoom over it

decision: a node card carries its kind's identity instead of a summary line
why: the old card was a labelled box; showing the icon, the kind's purpose, its own fields, and one labelled row per port is what makes a graph readable without opening the inspector
result: field edits from the card write through the store; edges attach to the named port rows

decision: flow node objects are reused while their rendered inputs are unchanged
why: React Flow keeps a node's measurement on the object it was handed and re-reads measured off the props, so a fresh object every render un-initialised the graph and no edge was ever drawn
result: the store shows measured width 300 and handle bounds set; edges render after any number of re-renders

decision: card geometry constants follow the wider card
why: NODE_WIDTH was still 220 from the old card, so an agent-added node landed flush against the previous column
result: Node 300x180; the seeded layouts moved to a 380px pitch, measured as an 80px gutter at 85 percent zoom

decision: the data catalogue appears only while a template field is in hand
why: it was a permanent right column and, once floating, it covered the cards its own copy tells you to click
result: no data panel on load; it appears when a template field is focused

decision: the validation list starts collapsed and no panel is open on load
why: the first view of a workflow should be the workflow
result: panel closed, pill reading no errors, and the Next dev badge off so it stops sitting over the pill in screenshots

decision: the builder agent moves onto Deep Agents with tools
why: one turn that pasted the whole graph and palette into the prompt could not look anything up and could not check its own work
result: 14-call turn: read, add, wire, re-read to verify, then point at the nodes it meant

decision: write tools collect operations; the applier stays the only authority
why: an agent with tools must still not be able to produce a definition the DSL rejects
result: applied 5, refused 0 on the live turn; a bad port is refused with the legal list

decision: a refused call and an unfinished graph are told apart
why: judging the whole plan on every call left the first refusal in the list, so every later call reported a mistake the agent had already fixed
result: adding a node reports "not valid yet"; a bad port reports "refused"

decision: the provider carries a conversation, not a flattened prompt
why: with every message flattened into one user turn the model could not tell a tool result from prose and answered by continuing the transcript
result: tool results arrive as tool turns; both transports map roles natively

decision: json mode is not requested when tools are declared
why: response_format json_object constrains the model to one JSON object, so it wrote JSON shaped like a tool call instead of making one
result: the same prompt that produced `{".read_workflow": {}}` now produces a real call

decision: models declare whether they call tools
why: measured against the vendor: v4.1-flash returns tool calls, v3.1 and v3.2 answer in prose
result: the chat runs on a model the catalogue says can use tools

decision: the builder agent summarizes its own history
why: one turn is a dozen model calls over a prompt carrying the kind catalogue, so a conversation that keeps its whole history re-sends all of it every turn: the measured turn cost 137k input tokens, most of them tool results the agent had already read
result: summarizer call fires past the threshold and the summary reaches the following calls; thresholds are ours because the harness defaults come from a model profile we do not ship

decision: the agent's trail and its focus are shown, and pointing is not selecting
why: an author who asks for a change gets a sentence and no account of how the agent got there, and a turn that says "these two approvals" leaves them hunting for which two
result: turn rendered pointed at 2 nodes / read_workflow {} / select_nodes {...}, both nodes ringed and framed; clicking a node cleared the ring and opened the inspector

decision: the end-to-end suite pins the provider instead of inheriting it
why: scenario B pinned the rules proposer and scenario A did not, so a demo left on the real vendor made the suite measure the network: a 41s ranking call spent the rejection test's 90s budget
result: with the tenant on the live vendor the suite now passes in 802ms and leaves the tenant on none

decision: a kind declares its inputs the way it declares its ports
why: outputs were declared and inputs were known by name: the card tested node.type !== 'trigger', the canvas tested it twice more, and the validator's only input rule was written against the isTrigger capability
result: trigger declares inputs: [] and every other kind declares one; INPUT_NOT_ACCEPTED replaces TRIGGER_HAS_INCOMING and no UI or validator code names the trigger as an input case

decision: inputs is an array with a ceiling pinned by a test
why: an edge names a source port and nothing else, so a kind declaring two inputs would be unaddressable
result: a kind with two inputs fails the registry test, which names the follow-up: edge grows toPort, React Flow edges grow targetHandle

decision: one port carries one target, and the validator now says so
why: the engine routes a node's outgoing edges through a map keyed by port, so a second edge on the same port overwrote the first: the definition validated and saved, then LangGraph refused to compile the graph because the replaced target had no incoming edge left
result: PORT_ALREADY_USED at save time and the same refusal from connect, instead of an UnreachableNodeError at run time

decision: one rule answers whether an edge may exist, and the canvas asks it
why: the applier, the validator and the canvas each held their own copy of the edge rules, and the canvas copy is the one no test can watch
result: edgeRefusal names the reason for a model or a person; nine tests cover it, including the ignore case the canvas needs when it re-checks an edge it is already drawing

decision: the agent node is a second kind, not a change to ai_decision
why: a loop changes the cost contract of every workflow already saved, and an audit wants a proposal whose cost is derivable from the definition
result: same declared tools and same structured output; the difference is that the model chooses the reads, up to maxSteps, and the run records the trail

decision: the adapter accepts the vendor's own function declaration
why: LangChain's structured-output strategy binds its extraction tool as {type:function,function:{name,description,parameters}}, which toolSpecOf rejected, so createAgent({responseFormat}) could not run at all
result: the same call that threw now returns a validated structuredResponse; a bound tool may be a LangChain tool, a {name,description,parameters} declaration, or a vendor function declaration

decision: a loop's tokens come from the model, not from the messages
why: when a loop throws, the graph returns no messages, so scanning them for usage recorded zero tokens for a loop that had already spent money
result: BuilderChatModel accumulates what the vendor reported and shares the accumulator with the copies bindTools makes; a failed loop now records its real tokens

decision: the loop prompt says a read is not a search
why: measured: the model called timesheet.get three times with identical arguments in one loop, spending a 3-step budget on nothing
result: the next run called each tool once and answered
